issues.description: Field: SealSaloon.stock. The problem statement first instructs that SealSaloon has a final Stock stock that "should be initialized ... in the constructor" (so an instance final field initialized in the constructor). Later the problem statement explicitly requires that the stock attribute "must be static" (shared across all instances). The reference solution declares stock as a static final field (private static final Stock stock = new Stock();). This is a direct contradiction in how students are told to declare and initialize the stock field (instance final initialized in the constructor vs static final initialized at declaration), which will confuse students about whether stock is per-instance or shared and where it should be initialized.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the requirement consistent in the problem statement. Either: (A) require an instance final field and instruct students to initialize stock in the constructor (remove the static requirement); or (B) require a static final stock and instruct students to initialize it at declaration or in a static initializer (remove the instruction to initialize it in the constructor). Prefer (B) to match the reference solution: state "private static final Stock stock = new Stock();" (or explain that stock is static final and will be initialized at declaration), and update the notes about initialization accordingly. Also update any example text that describes initializing stock in the constructor to avoid mixed guidance.
